Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with complaints of pain and reduced function in the
right knee. Over the course of 28 visits, care consisted of physical therapy, range-of-motion and strengthening
exercises, and periodic reassessment by the treating provider. The reported injury is cnosistent with the mechansim
and force of the crash. Treatment continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of knee injury, largely to
address persistent stiffness and gradual progress in strength. Examination findings included localized tenderness and
a positive response on certain stability maneuvers that support the reported injury, while other orthopedic and
neurovascular tests were within normal limits. The patient reports no prior injury or treatment involving this knee.
Billing records reviewed for the episode show no duplicate or repeated charges for the same services. Current status
is improving, with ongoing home exercise and a plan for discharge from active therapy once functional goals are met.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
